sweep_summary: Kabardian (kaba1278): this search of works with stress in the title found exactly one title-matched work, Applebaum 2013 'Prosody and Grammar in Kabardian' (UCSB PhD, already listed as wanted). Its abstract, obtained from the Google Books record (no preview; ProQuest ISBN 9781303424557), shows the dissertation is about prosodic units above the word (prosodic word, intonation unit, prosodic sentence) predicted from finite/non-finite verb distinctions, and is silent on word-stress placement; the held 2023 chapter cites it only for morphology, fusion and phrase-level prosody. No open copy exists: a full OAI-PMH harvest of eScholarship's ucsb set (18,878 records) has no deposit, Semantic Scholar lists no OA PDF, and Gordon's author page posts six Kabardian papers but not the thesis; ProQuest and the library aggregators were unreachable (error/bot-challenge pages) by automated download. Priority medium: it would at most corroborate the CVV/CVC-final-else-penult rule already held first-hand from Gordon & Applebaum 2010 (JIPA sec. 2.3 pp. 37-38; Phonology p. 50) and 2023 (sec. 15.4.1), which remain the best statements; the catalog's Colarusso 1992 deciding source and the pending reclassify (weight-hedged -> weight-sensitive) are unaffected. Evidence and logged in there.

new_statements.quote: Phonological descriptions of Kabardian are in agreement that stress characteristically falls on either the penultimate or the final syllable of a word (Turchaninov & Tsagov 1940; Yakovlev 1948; Abitov et al 1957; Colarusso 1992, 2006): the final syllable if it is heavy, i.e. contains either a long vowel (CVV) or a coda consonant (CVC), and the penult if the final syllable is light. ... Colarusso (1992: 16) observes that stress fails to fall on nominal suffixes, although he also notes that certain suffixes can carry a secondary stress. Verbal suffixes, on the other hand, can carry primary stress as long as they 'are of a purely verbal character' (p. 17).

sources.citation: Gordon, Matthew & Ayla Applebaum. 2010. Prosodic fusion and minimality in Kabardian. Phonology 27: 45-76. doi:10.1017/S0952675710000035 (author-posted copy).
sources.quote: 'The prosodic word is the domain of stress assignment in Kabardian. Stress is phonologically predictable (Abitov et al. 1957, Colarusso 1992, 2006), falling on a final heavy syllable (CVV, CVC), otherwise on the penult.' p.53: 'In all forms displaying fusion, stress follows the predictable Kabardian pattern, according to which the final syllable is stressed if heavy, otherwise the penult is stressed.'
sources.note: Defines the prosodic word as stress domain and restates the weight rule; supports domain=prosodic word rather than 'last stem morpheme'. downloaded now.

sources.citation: Frolova, Anastasia Vadimovna. 2024. Prosodic markers of the state of "joy" (using the example of linguistic realizations of Kabardian Bilinguals in the Caucasian Mineral Waters region). Philology. Theory & Practice 17(6): 1809-1814. doi:10.30853/phil20240258
sources.locator: p. 1812; Table 1 and interpretation p. 1811; conclusions p. 1813
sources.note: The article compares the Russian speech of Kabardian bilinguals with that of Russians in 'joy' dialogues and finds the accented Russian has a higher tonal register, wider rising and falling F0 intervals, a rising phrase end, longer and more open/back vowels and larger loudness swings. It states nothing about word stress, accent or tone in Kabardian; the one sentence on Kabardian (that it 'may' use vowel duration distinctively) is a speculation from the accented-Russian vowel durations, not a description of the language.

sources.quote: This study provides a systematic phonetic analysis of the basic entities of Kabardian prosodic units above the word and investigates the predictability of prosodic units from grammatical and discourse factors. ... Kabardian prosodic units of various sizes are hierarchically arranged with the syllable being the smallest constituent followed in order of increasing size by the prosodic word, the intonation unit and the prosodic sentence. The salient morphosyntactic correlate of the two largest units is the distinction between finite and non-finite verbs.
sources.note: Glottolog-listed full-length study of Kabardian prosody (morphological slot structure, prosodic word, intonation); would be the most detailed source for the stress-domain/affix clause. eScholarship and UCSB ADRL could not be reached by automated download; likely ProQuest.
